name: Shimla
imageAlt: Shimla's houses stacked along a forested ridge under a clear sky
summary: The old summer capital: colonial streets on a ridge, cedar forest walks and an easy drive or toy-train ride from the plains.
highlights: Walk the Mall Road and the Ridge at sunset
Christ Church and the Gaiety Theatre
Jakhu Temple through the cedar forest
Day trip to Kufri and the Mahasu peak trail
Viceregal Lodge (Indian Institute of Advanced Study)
Cafés and bakeries on Lakkar Bazaar
cautions: [1,2] Snow can close roads around Kufri in January and February.

name: Manali
imageAlt: Snowfields and a winding valley high in the Himachal Himalaya
summary: Pine valleys, the Beas river and the gateway to high passes. Paragliding, rafting and snow in season.
highlights: Old Manali lanes and the Hadimba Devi temple
Solang Valley: paragliding or the ropeway
Atal Tunnel and a snow stop at Sissu
Naggar Castle and the Roerich Gallery
Café evenings on Old Manali road
cautions: [11,12,1,2,3,4,5] Rohtang Pass is closed from November to May; the Atal Tunnel and Sissu usually stay open.
[6,7,8,9,10] Rohtang Pass needs an online permit booked in advance.

name: Kasol
imageAlt: Trekkers crossing a snowy ridge above the Parvati valley
summary: A riverside village in the Parvati valley with cheap stays, forest trails and the overnight Kheerganga trek.
highlights: Kheerganga trek with a night at the top
cautions: The Kheerganga trek is 12 km each way; plan a full day for it.

name: Dharamshala & McLeod Ganj
imageAlt: Blue Himalayan ridges and pine slopes at first light
summary: Home of the Dalai Lama's temple, Tibetan cafés and the Triund ridge walk, with the Dhauladhar range as backdrop.
highlights: Tsuglagkhang, the Dalai Lama's temple complex
Triund trek for sunset over the Dhauladhars

name: Rishikesh
imageAlt: A clear mountain river running through forest in the Garhwal foothills
summary: Yoga ashrams, the Ganga aarti and white-water rafting, all within a few kilometres of each other.
highlights: Evening Ganga aarti at Parmarth Niketan or Triveni Ghat
Walk across Ram Jhula and the Lakshman Jhula area
Morning yoga class at an ashram
Day trip to Haridwar's Har Ki Pauri
cautions: [7,8] Rafting stops in July and August when the river is in flood.

name: Nainital
imageAlt: Rowing boats on Naini Lake with the town climbing the hills behind
summary: A lake town in the Kumaon hills: boating, ropeway views of the Himalaya and quieter lakes nearby.
highlights: Naina Devi temple and the Mall Road
Day trip to Bhimtal and Sattal

name: Kedarnath
imageAlt: Kedarnath temple's stone facade with pilgrims and peaks behind
summary: One of the Char Dham shrines, reached by a 16 km trek from Gaurikund. Open roughly May to early November.
highlights: Drive to Sonprayag and register for the yatra
Trek from Gaurikund to Kedarnath (16 km)
Kedarnath temple darshan and evening aarti
Trek down and night halt at Guptkashi
cautions: The temple is closed in winter. Registration on the Uttarakhand tourism portal is mandatory.
The trek is strenuous at altitude; ponies and helicopter tickets cost extra.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
imageAlt: Close-up of a leopard's face and pale eyes
summary: India's oldest national park: jeep safaris through sal forest and grassland in search of tigers, elephants and birds.
highlights: Morning jeep safari in Bijrani or Jhirna zone
Afternoon safari in a second zone
Garjiya Devi temple on the Kosi river
cautions: [11,12,1,2] Safari permits sell out early in winter; book on the official Corbett site.
[6,7,8,9,10] Most core zones close from mid-June to mid-October.

name: Leh, Ladakh
imageAlt: A rider on an empty highway through the bare mountains of Ladakh
summary: High desert, monasteries and some of the world's highest motorable passes. Needs time to acclimatise.
highlights: Rest day in Leh to acclimatise; Shanti Stupa at sunset
Leh Palace and the old town
Day trip over Khardung La to Nubra Valley
Magnetic Hill and the Sangam confluence
cautions: Leh is at 3,500 m. Keep the first full day for rest; altitude sickness is common.
Inner Line Permits are required for Nubra and Pangong.

name: Srinagar
imageAlt: Wooden houseboats moored on Dal Lake with snow-capped mountains behind
summary: Houseboats on Dal Lake, Mughal gardens and day trips to the meadows of Gulmarg and Sonamarg.
highlights: Shikara ride on Dal Lake at dawn
Day trip to Gulmarg and the gondola
Old city: Jamia Masjid and Shah-e-Hamadan
Sonamarg and the Thajiwas glacier walk
cautions: [3,4] The Tulip Garden blooms only for a few weeks from late March to April.

name: Pahalgam
imageAlt: A horse grazing in a green meadow below snowy Kashmir peaks
summary: Meadows, pine forest and the Lidder river. Ponies up to Baisaran and the Aru and Betaab valleys.

name: Amritsar
imageAlt: The Golden Temple reflected in the sacred pool at dusk
summary: The Golden Temple at dawn and after dark, the langar kitchen that feeds thousands, and some of India's best street food.
highlights: Golden Temple before dawn and again after dark
Langar at the Guru Ram Das kitchen
Beating Retreat ceremony at the Attari–Wagah border
Kulcha and lassi crawl in the old city

name: Agra
imageAlt: The Taj Mahal framed by a red sandstone archway
summary: The Taj Mahal at sunrise, the Agra Fort and Akbar's abandoned city at Fatehpur Sikri.
highlights: Mehtab Bagh for the Taj across the river at sunset
Petha and bedai breakfast in Kinari Bazaar
cautions: The Taj Mahal is closed to visitors on Fridays.

name: Delhi
imageAlt: India Gate under a pink and violet evening sky
summary: Mughal monuments, Lutyens' avenues and the best food city in the north, from Old Delhi stalls to Mehrauli rooftops.
highlights: Old Delhi: Jama Masjid and a Chandni Chowk food walk
Qutub Minar and Mehrauli Archaeological Park
India Gate and Kartavya Path at dusk
cautions: [11,12,1] Air quality is often poor from November to January.

name: Jaipur
imageAlt: Hawa Mahal's pink honeycomb facade above a busy Jaipur street
summary: The Pink City: hilltop forts, palace courtyards and bazaars for block prints and gemstones.
highlights: Hawa Mahal and the old-city bazaars
Dinner at Chokhi Dhani or a Rajasthani thali

name: Udaipur
imageAlt: Udaipur's City Palace glowing gold above Lake Pichola
summary: The city of lakes: palace views from rooftop cafés, sunset boats on Pichola and quiet lanes around Gangaur Ghat.
highlights: Bagore ki Haveli evening dance show

name: Jaisalmer
imageAlt: Golden sandstone fort walls in the Rajasthan desert
summary: A living sandstone fort in the Thar, carved havelis, and a night under the stars at the Sam dunes.
highlights: Inside Jaisalmer Fort's lanes and Jain temples
Camel ride and sunset at Sam sand dunes
cautions: [3,4,5,6,7,8,9] Afternoons are very hot; plan sightseeing for early morning and evening.

name: Varanasi
imageAlt: Wooden boats moored at the Varanasi ghats at dusk
summary: The oldest living city on the Ganga: sunrise boats along the ghats, the evening aarti and the lanes around Kashi Vishwanath.
highlights: Sunrise boat ride from Assi to Manikarnika
Walk the ghats from Assi to Panchganga
Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught
Kachori, lassi and paan in the old lanes
Banaras Hindu University and Bharat Kala Bhavan

name: Ujjain
imageAlt: Riverside ghats and moored boats at dusk
summary: Home of Mahakaleshwar, one of the twelve jyotirlingas, with the Mahakal Lok corridor and ghats on the Shipra.
highlights: Ram Ghat evening aarti on the Shipra
cautions: Bhasma Aarti needs advance online booking.
[7,8] July–August (Shravan) is extremely crowded.

name: Omkareshwar
imageAlt: A burning orange evening sky over open country
summary: A jyotirlinga temple on an island in the Narmada, with a parikrama path around it and the new Statue of Oneness.
highlights: Ekatmata Dham, the Statue of Oneness

name: Pachmarhi
imageAlt: Mist rolling over forested hills in soft morning light
summary: Madhya Pradesh's only hill station: sandstone gorges, waterfalls and cave shrines in the Satpura range.
highlights: Gypsy safari to Apsara Vihar and Rajat Prapat
Satpura Tiger Reserve boat safari at Madhai

name: Goa
imageAlt: A curve of palm-lined beach in Goa with clear turquoise water
summary: Beaches for every mood, from Baga's parties to Palolem's calm, plus Portuguese-era churches and seafood shacks.
highlights: North Goa beaches: Anjuna, Vagator and Chapora Fort at sunset
Old Goa churches: Bom Jesus and Sé Cathedral
Water sports at Calangute or Baga
Seafood thali at a beach shack
cautions: [6,7,8,9] Most beach shacks close and sea swimming is unsafe from June to September.
[12,1] Prices spike sharply between Christmas and New Year.

name: Gokarna
imageAlt: Soft waves on an empty beach at sunset
summary: A temple town with a string of quiet coves linked by a clifftop trail. Calmer and cheaper than Goa.
highlights: Mahabaleshwar temple and the old car street
Beach trek: Kudle to Om to Half Moon to Paradise
cautions: [6,7,8,9] The sea is rough and many cafés close in the monsoon.

name: Varkala
imageAlt: Turquoise sea breaking on dark rocks below a seafront walkway
summary: Red laterite cliffs above a long beach, with cafés along the cliff edge and Ayurvedic treatments everywhere.
highlights: Clifftop walk from North Cliff to Black Beach

name: Alappuzha (Alleppey)
imageAlt: A thatched houseboat gliding along a palm-fringed Kerala backwater
summary: Kerala's backwaters: a night on a houseboat, canoe trips through village canals and toddy-shop lunches.
highlights: Shikara or country-boat ride through narrow canals
cautions: [12,1] Houseboat prices jump over Christmas–New Year; book early.

name: Munnar
imageAlt: Mist drifting across steep green hills in the Western Ghats
summary: Rolling tea estates at 1,600 m, cool days all year and walks through cardamom and cloud forest.
highlights: Tea Museum and a factory visit
Eravikulam National Park for the Nilgiri tahr
cautions: [6,7,8] Heavy monsoon rain from June to August can trigger landslides.

name: Coorg (Kodagu)
imageAlt: Mist rolling over forested hills in soft morning light
summary: Coffee estates, homestays with Kodava cooking and waterfalls in the forested hills of southern Karnataka.
highlights: Pandi curry dinner at a homestay

name: Ooty
imageAlt: Mist drifting across steep green hills in the Nilgiris
summary: The Nilgiris' classic hill station: a UNESCO-listed mountain railway, botanical gardens and tea country.
highlights: Coonoor tea estates and Sim's Park

name: Mysuru
imageAlt: Mysore Palace's domes and arches against a blue sky
summary: A gracious palace city: the illuminated Mysore Palace, Chamundi Hill and Devaraja market's flowers and spices.
highlights: Mysore Palace (lit up on Sunday evenings)
Chamundi Hill and the Nandi statue
Srirangapatna fort and Tipu's summer palace
Mysore pak and masala dosa at a classic café
cautions: [9,10] Dasara in October brings spectacular crowds and higher prices.

name: Hampi
imageAlt: The towering Virupaksha temple gopuram among Hampi's boulders
summary: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital scattered across a boulder landscape. Best explored by bicycle.
highlights: Vittala temple and the stone chariot

name: Puducherry
imageAlt: Soft waves on an empty beach at sunset
summary: French Quarter streets in mustard and white, the seafront Promenade, cafés and the Auroville community.
highlights: Walk the White Town and the Promenade at dawn
Auroville and the Matrimandir viewing point
cautions: [10,11] The north-east monsoon brings heavy rain, mostly in November.

name: Madurai
imageAlt: A brightly painted South Indian temple tower at dusk
summary: The Meenakshi Amman temple's painted towers at the heart of one of India's oldest cities, with a famous night food scene.
highlights: Meenakshi Amman temple (and the night ceremony)

name: Hyderabad
imageAlt: The Charminar rising above a crowded old-city street in Hyderabad
summary: Biryani, Irani chai and the Qutb Shahi city: Charminar's bazaars, Golconda Fort and the Chowmahalla Palace.
highlights: Golconda Fort at sunset with the light show
Biryani and Irani chai with Osmania biscuits

name: Mumbai
imageAlt: Marine Drive's seafront promenade curving past Mumbai's towers
summary: Gateway of India, art deco Marine Drive, Bandra's cafés and vada pav at every corner.
highlights: Gateway of India and the Taj Mahal Palace
Street food at Juhu or Girgaum Chowpatty
cautions: [6,7,8,9] Heavy monsoon rain can flood streets and disrupt local trains.

name: Lonavala & Khandala
imageAlt: Mist rolling over forested hills in soft morning light
summary: The Sahyadri escape between Mumbai and Pune: monsoon waterfalls, hill forts and chikki.
highlights: Tiger's Leap and Lion's Point viewpoints
Chikki and fudge on the main bazaar
cautions: [6,7,8,9] Monsoon weekends are packed and roads to viewpoints jam up.

name: Kolkata
imageAlt: Howrah Bridge lit gold at night over the Hooghly river
summary: Colonial grandeur, College Street books, the Hooghly ghats and some of the country's best sweets.
highlights: Howrah Bridge and the flower market at dawn
College Street and Indian Coffee House
Dakshineswar and Belur Math by ferry
cautions: [9,10] Durga Puja is spectacular but very crowded.

name: Puri
imageAlt: Soft waves on an empty beach at sunset
summary: The Jagannath temple, a long Bay of Bengal beach and day trips to Konark's Sun Temple.
cautions: Non-Hindus are not permitted inside the Jagannath temple.
[6,7] Rath Yatra draws enormous crowds.

name: Darjeeling
imageAlt: Darjeeling's hillside town with clouds pouring over the ridges beyond
summary: Tea gardens, the toy train and dawn views of Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill.
highlights: Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill
Darjeeling Himalayan Railway joyride to Ghum
Padmaja Naidu Zoo and the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute

name: Gangtok
imageAlt: A gilded Buddhist monastery roof above misty Himalayan valleys
summary: Sikkim's tidy capital: monasteries, MG Marg's evening stroll and day trips to high lakes.
highlights: Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir (permit day trip)
Momos and thukpa at a local canteen
cautions: Tsomgo Lake and Nathula need permits arranged through a registered agent.

name: Andaman Islands
imageAlt: White sand and clear turquoise water under leaning palms
summary: Port Blair's history, then ferries to Havelock's Radhanagar beach and coral reefs for snorkelling and diving.
highlights: Cellular Jail and the evening sound-and-light show
Snorkelling or a discover-scuba dive at Elephant Beach
cautions: Island ferries need booking ahead and can be cancelled in rough weather.
